why: Matching pairs with a twist: keep a stack of indices whose bottom is the position of the last unmatched ')' (start with -1). When a ')' matches, the current valid run reaches back to the index now on top, so its length is i - top. It needs the matching-pairs stack plus the sentinel insight.
hints: When a ')' at i matches, where does the valid substring ending at i start?
Just after the most recent index that is still unmatched: either an unmatched '(' still on the stack, or the last ')' that could not be matched.
Stack of indices initialised to [-1]. '(' pushes i. ')' pops; if the stack is now empty, push i as the new barrier, else best = max(best, i - stack[-1]). O(n).
pitfalls: "()()" is valid as a whole: adjacent valid pieces join, which the sentinel handles automatically.
Counting matched pairs is not enough; they must be contiguous.
